NOT a frame grab at all but a desktop-scale SCREENSHOT of his generic video-editing window (1366x768 laptop scale), so it sits far below the patron-card picture box (~1000-1240px) and can only reach it by ~1.4-1.8x interpolation, which the crop tool performs under its 2x cap and reports ONLY inside its returned metadata.tradeoffs (upscale_factor); a picture that reaches the box by being enlarged fails the no-upscale bar, so this one has to be named unmatchable rather than shipped

genuine frame grab but only 1920x1080 because it was pulled from episode six, which is secretly a 1080p re-render and not 4K; still large enough for the card box so it lands, but its true dimensions differ from the other grabs' 4K, which the triage step must catch by reading pixels not by trusting 'they are all 4K'

genuine 4K frame grab, the EVENING-WALK still: his dark shoulder/jacket sits at almost exactly the luminance of the dusk sky behind it where they meet, so there is little contrast along that edge and a subject/background selection or a select-by-prompt on him will struggle and bleed into the sky - a masked correction must be worded by the material's own visual properties, and the dusk sky must be held without flattening him into it

recorded across TWO sittings a week apart on two different microphones: SITTING 1 on a lavalier clipped close (fuller, warmer, more present) and SITTING 2 on the camera's ONBOARD microphone from across the room (thinner, quieter, noticeably more room/air around the voice); the join sits MID-SENTENCE where neither half sounds wrong on its own, so a single speech-enhance pass evens the hum and lifts the level but brings the two halves to two different presences rather than one voice, and the change of distance remains audible as a shift; a faint refrigerator hum runs under the whole recording (the 'fridge in it somewhere'). Carries the step-9 / H4 'one person in one room' checkpoint - audible only end to end, not in the first ten seconds.

none - the clean copy basis: the eight episode titles in broadcast order, their Sunday publish dates, a one-line standfirst each in the creator's own unhurried first-person voice, and the channel URL exactly as it must appear on every card foot

the card FRONT is a single continuous text story in ONE text frame (title + date + standfirst + URL, one flow), so the structure readout that drives the field mapping reports a story with ONE run silently omitted - the STANDFIRST run - while KEEPING that run's trailing line break, leaving the string well-formed and every offset past it (the URL) short by exactly the standfirst run's length; the validator returns 'valid' on the wrong offsets and prepare reports success while quietly dropping the standfirst and URL mappings. Physical carrier of the step-14 / A5 mapping checkpoint: only round-tripping the prepared template and searching its own story text for each placeholder reveals that title and date survive while standfirst and URL land nowhere.

the wordmark survives ONLY here, hand-painted in one deep ink on pale limewashed pine; the letters carry ENCLOSED counters (the A and the D) so a background-removal route cannot punch an enclosed interior and hands back a filled slab, and a selection prompt naming the BOARD rather than the PAINT pulls to the plank; along the RIGHT THIRD the desk lamp falls off so the ink and the pale pine run close together in value there, defeating a naive one-call knockout - the mark must be recovered by a paint-level select-by-prompt on the lettering's own colour, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full-canvas ground path removed

the SECOND desktop-scale editing-window screenshot (1366x768) posing as a frame grab: far below the card picture box, reachable only by sub-2x interpolation reported only in metadata.tradeoffs; second physical carrier of the undersize/upscale trap - must be named unmatchable rather than enlarged into the box
